newsitem.title: UK: IPE OIL FUTURES FIRMER, LOOKING TECHNICALLY BULLISH.
newsitem.headline: IPE OIL FUTURES FIRMER, LOOKING TECHNICALLY BULLISH.

text.p: IPE crude and gas oil were firmer in early trade with both contracts extending Wednesday's NYMEX gasoline-led gains, though both are looking technically bullish in their own right, traders and analysts said said.
By 0941 GMT September Brent which expires at close of business today stood 10 cents higher at $19.09 a barrel, with the October contract up four cents at $19.20 a barrel.
September gas oil was up $2.50 at $172.50 a tonne.
"Brent looks technically bullish although I am more bullish WTI where there is more evidence of strong local demand," Tom James, analyst at Credit Lyonnaise Rouse said.
Brent's trading action on Tuesday continued a short-term trend of higher highs and higher lows stemming from last Friday's dip to $18.28.

This pattern is usually deemed bullish and is also coupled with a pennant or flag formation on the spot month chart which may signal the resumption of the market's the bullish trend from July 21 to August 7.
Analysts said the September gas oil contract was now starting to look slightly bullish after the recent five trading day bearish trend.
"After holding the 50 percent retracement level on Monday and recovering it looks more positive," James said.
"I would become very bullish if we could see the trading gap $171 to $172 filled and break and close above $172."
